cards.explanation: The answer is that the LORD God of Israel has entered through it. Verse 2 says, “…because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered through it.” Then comes the last line: “Therefore it will remain shut.” No construction crew, no battle, just the fact that He came through that gate. That's the whole reason, friends, and the text gives it plainly.

The answer is the prince. Verse 3 says, “Only the prince himself may sit inside the gateway to eat in the presence of the LORD.” He comes in by the portico of the gateway and goes out the same way. A shut gate with exactly one name on the guest list, friends.

The answer is facedown. Ezekiel the prophet looked, saw the glory of the LORD filling His temple, and says, “…I fell facedown.” That's what he did when he saw it. Friends, the glory fills the temple, and down he goes.

The answer is all the laws of the house of the LORD. The LORD tells Ezekiel to listen closely to “…everything I tell you concerning all the statutes and laws of the house of the LORD.” He also says to take careful note of the entrance to the temple and all the exits of the sanctuary. He asks Ezekiel to look carefully with his eyes and listen closely with his ears.

The answer is foreigners uncircumcised in heart and flesh. The LORD says, “…you brought in foreigners uncircumcised in both heart and flesh to occupy My sanctuary…” Notice He says both heart and flesh, friends. That's on top of all their other abominations.

The answer is False. God says, “And you have not kept charge of My holy things, but have appointed others to keep charge of My sanctuary for you.” So Israel didn't keep charge of the holy things themselves, friends. They appointed others to do it.

The answer is True, and the verse leaves no gap. The Lord GOD says, “No foreigner uncircumcised in heart and flesh may enter My sanctuary…” Then He adds that this includes even a foreigner who lives among the Israelites. Living next door doesn't change it, friends.

The answer is False. God says of these Levites, “Yet they shall be ministers in My sanctuary…” They will have charge of the temple gates and slaughter the burnt offerings and other sacrifices for the people. They still bear the consequences, friends, but they're still given work to do in His sanctuary.

The answer is priests. God says of the Levites who ministered before idols, “They must not approach Me to serve Me as priests…” They also can't come near any of His holy things or the most holy things. Then God says He will appoint them to keep charge of all the work for the temple (Ezekiel 44:14).

The answer is that they kept charge of His sanctuary. God says these Levitical priests, descended from Zadok, are the ones “…who kept charge of My sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from Me…” Because of that, they are to approach Him and minister before Him. They kept charge while Israel went astray, friends.

The answer is True. After naming the priests descended from Zadok, God says, “They alone shall enter My sanctuary and draw near to My table to minister before Me.” That word “alone” does the work, friends. They will keep His charge.

The answer is to teach the difference between holy and common. God says, “They are to teach My people the difference between the holy and the common…” He adds that they're to show the people how to discern between the clean and the unclean. So they serve before Him, friends, and they also teach the people.

The answer is True. God says, “In any dispute, they shall officiate as judges and judge according to My ordinances.” So the priests aren't judging by their own ideas, friends, but by His ordinances. They also keep His laws for all His appointed feasts and keep His Sabbaths holy.

The answer is God Himself. God says, “In regard to their inheritance, I am their inheritance.” Then He says to give them no possession in Israel, “…for I am their possession.” Imagine that, friends: no land, and God Himself as the inheritance.

The answer is so a blessing may rest on their homes. Verse 30 says, “You are to give your first batch of dough to the priest, so that a blessing may rest upon your homes.” That's the reason the text gives, friends. As a cookie man, I've got a lot of respect for a first batch.
